function: Excluded (system): jammer-aided secure and private OTA-FL aggregation design (an area 7 problem) over scalar-gain links, with no antenna array and no RIS (pp. 4, 11).
notes: Excluded at the system check. The earlier checks pass: it is a research article; as OTA-FL it passes the learning check by rule (the CNN trained across the devices, p. 11: "training a convolutional neural network (CNN) on the popular MNIST dataset"); and the problem is the design of the over-the-air aggregation itself (scheduling of learners and jammers, power scaling and post-processing factor, minimizing the aggregation error under privacy and security constraints), which is area 7. The link is a scalar-gain multiple access channel: p. 4: "are the channel gain coefficients linking device n with the BS and the eavesdropper" (real gains in R+, eqs. (5)-(6)); p. 4: "via a shared MAC". The word antenna never appears in the paper, MIMO appears only in reference titles (p. 15), and RIS or IRS only in a reference title and an author biography (p. 16), so there is no array and no RIS. The paper does not state the number of antennas, so the exclusion rests on this scalar channel model; if the reviewer requires an explicit single-antenna statement, the work would be an area 7 inclusion. In that case: no standard or measured channel and no open data (q1 and q5 would be 0, only MNIST is used, p. 11); no test in new conditions (q2 would be 0); baselines are the earlier non-learned designs NoJ [29] and power scaling PS [18] (p. 11); complexity orders O(N^4) for SU and O(N^2) for the LC scheme are given (pp. 8-9). Quantitative results exist (Figs. 2-6, pp. 11-12), so the results check is not the reason.
